ctx.x: who you -- they called him Floorshow, at this session.
Floorshow, you'd be playing and all of a sudden, Floorshow would jump out and do a flip-flop with this horn and start a honking and break the house up and then, he has won the battle.

So, Don (inaudible Byas) had watched Floorshow for a few times when he'd been doing that so, this was another of them sessions, tenor saxophone sessions, so, they was playing 'Cherokee' and everybody was happy, you know, all of a sudden, Floorshow jumps out and does his flip-flop -- (verbally demonstrating).

items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: I met him in a place called Beefsteak Charlie's and Don was so frantic, I said, well, Don, come on, let me buy you something to drink.

ctx.x: Well, what you were saying, how did Young strike you when you heard him, first heard him?

Well, Lester Young struck me as a -- first, I heard him play the clarinet. See, I heard him play in Moten's band the clarinet and I heard him -- Herschel Evans play the tenor saxophone. And Herschel Evans, see, Herschel Evans had lived what it seemed like, because Chu Berry had been around there and Don Byas had been around there a long time. And before Don Byas died, he was playing all of that complete music, because he went and stuck to a course of harmony and theory. He was a valedictorian. When he come out of…
So, Lester Young, he struck me first, he was, he had decided that I'm going to shock people intentionally.
